newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir journalists end government boycott.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir journalists end government boycott.

text.p: Journalists in troubled Kashmir decided on Thursday to end a nearly month-long boycott of all Indian government functions after the transfer of three police officials accused of using undue force against reporters.

"The 27-day-old boycott of government functions by journalists in Kashmir ended today following the official order shifting the three police officials accused of beating journalists," the Kashmiri Journalists Union said in a statement.

At least 20 Kashmiri journalists were injured on June 27 when police fired tear gas and used batons to control protesters demonstrating against the alleged use of police force against journalists covering a women's demonstration.
More than 50 Kashmir-based journalists then decided to boycott all government functions and disregard official statements unless the three accused police officials were suspended.
Chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir state Farooq Abdullah has ordered an enquiry into the incident.
Kashmiri journalists have been the targets of attacks by both separatist guerrillas and security forces during the seven-year-old separatist revolt in the Himalayan region.
At least six journalists have been killed in Kashmir since the insurgency erupted in 1990, and dozens have escaped attempts on their lives by unidentified gunmen.

Militants supporting Indian control over Kashmir took 19 journalists hostage last July and threatened to kill four unless their editors agreed to meet them. The hostages were later rescued by the Indian army.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting for independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan, and at least three pro-India groups are helping paramilitary troops combat militancy.
